# Abderrahmane Wardi

### Professor of Electrical Engineering · PhD Candidate

I am **Abderrahmane Wardi**, a Professor of **Electrical Engineering and Industrial Engineering Sciences** and a PhD candidate at **École Nationale Supérieure d'Arts et Métiers (ENSAM), Mohammed V University in Rabat, Morocco**.

My academic background is primarily in **electrical engineering**, with teaching and technical activities spanning **embedded systems, signal processing, instrumentation, automation, electrical systems, and industrial engineering sciences**.

My doctoral research extends these engineering areas toward **biomedical applications**, particularly **ECG signal processing, intelligent biomedical instrumentation, TinyML, and embedded artificial intelligence**.

## Teaching

My teaching activities focus on **electrical engineering and industrial engineering sciences**, including topics related to:

- signal acquisition and processing;
- sensors and instrumentation;
- electronics;
- automatic control;
- embedded systems;
- electrical systems;
- industrial systems;
- communication and information processing.

This website provides course materials, tutorials, exercises, laboratory activities, technical documents, and educational resources for students.

[Explore Teaching Resources](teaching.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Research

My research activities are rooted in **electrical engineering, signal processing, embedded systems, and intelligent instrumentation**.

My doctoral research particularly investigates the application of these engineering disciplines to **biomedical systems**, with current interests including:

- ECG signal processing and analysis;
- embedded biomedical systems;
- TinyML for biomedical applications;
- embedded artificial intelligence;
- intelligent biomedical instrumentation;
- Edge AI;
- IoT for healthcare.

[Explore Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Research Projects

Current and recent projects include the development of intelligent embedded systems for signal acquisition, processing, classification, and monitoring.

These projects combine several areas of electrical engineering, including **electronics, embedded computing, digital signal processing, communication systems, instrumentation, and artificial intelligence**.

[View Projects](projects.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
